trigger: irreversible operations (writes to CHANGELOG drops and a run-state file that pins a permanent release date) + cross-plugin path resolution (release_paths -> shipwright-run orchestrator)

doubts.claim_under_doubt: A stored state is reused only for an interrupted release, so the stored date is always the right date.
doubts.disproof_attempt: `prepare` saves the state unconditionally, before any preview, question or aggregate. `resolve` reuses any stored state with the same version, no tag and an age under 48h. Failing case: on Monday an operator runs prepare for 1.3.0, previews, and abandons. On Tuesday the real release runs prepare again, gets Monday's date back, and `aggregate` renders `## [1.3.0] - <Monday>`. Under the old prose an unpassed date defaulted to today.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Reuse the stored date only when a real aggregate has already run for that version, or when `## [version]` is already in CHANGELOG.md; otherwise take today's date and keep only the run id.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: A page that already has its upgrade-note drop writes nothing on a re-run, even after the model has reworded it.
doubts.disproof_attempt: `_run_id` keeps '.' in the run id. `write_changelog_drop.py` names the file with `sanitize_run_id_for_filename`, which turns '.' into '-'. `_has_drop` globs the unsanitized id, so a page named `v0.36-split.md` never matches its own drop, and after a model edit a later prepare writes a second drop with the original wording.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Glob with the sanitized id, or strip '.' in `_run_id`. Add a test with a dotted page name.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The CLI driver's traces equal the frozen traces, so behaviour is preserved.
doubts.disproof_attempt: driver_cli.py records `out_of_sequence: asked` whenever the warning is set and never reads `gates.out_of_sequence`; it always passes an explicit `--release-date`, so the stored-date default path (A6) never runs in any golden scenario.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Derive out_of_sequence from the gates answer, add a scenario without --release-date, or state explicitly that A6 is covered by L1 tests only.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The golden-lock delta for coverage.py is an operator-approved change.
doubts.disproof_attempt: The BRIEF P3 row lists inventory.json in its touch set, not the frozen coverage.py. The approved_deltas.json entry justifies itself by inference and was written in the same diff.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Point to the operator decision that covers editing coverage.py, or flag it for the operator at the next stop.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The run-state write is atomic and safe.
doubts.disproof_attempt: The temp name is fixed (`release_run.json.tmp`); two overlapping release.py calls in one checkout can make the second os.replace fail.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Use a unique temp name and report an OSError as JSON, or rebut: one release per checkout is serial by contract.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: The page's own words make a correct changelog bullet.
doubts.disproof_attempt: No injection found (argv element, newlines flattened). Quality: real pages yield bullets that drop list items after a colon or double the link; a 400-character cut can split a backtick.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Accept as designed, since the model reviews the drop.

disposition: medium 1 fixed (unrendered state from an earlier day takes today's date); medium 2 fixed (run id has no dots); low 5 fixed (per-process temp name); low 3, 4, 6 accepted and recorded in FINDINGS D27/D31.
